meta.name: Mirofish
meta.tagline: A local MCP bridge that lets Claude Code control TradingView Desktop — read charts, run backtests, and build indicators from natural-language commands.

summary: Mirofish is a local MCP bridge that connects Claude Code to TradingView Desktop using the Chrome DevTools Protocol, letting an AI drive the platform with natural-language commands.

It's asset-agnostic — anything TradingView charts, it can drive: stocks, crypto, futures, FX. The integration reads charts, switches symbols and timeframes, writes Pine Script, runs backtests, creates alerts, manages drawings, captures screenshots, uses replay mode, and builds custom indicators directly in TradingView.
It's an open-source demo of how AI can automate TradingView workflows. It's an unofficial integration that relies on internal interfaces, and may stop working if TradingView updates its platform.

architecture: A local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes TradingView actions as tools that Claude Code can call.
The bridge speaks to TradingView Desktop over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) — the same low-level interface dev tooling uses to inspect and automate a Chromium app — to read and drive the UI.
Because it's an unofficial integration built on internal interfaces, it can break when TradingView ships UI changes; it is a demonstration of agentic automation, not a supported product.
caveats: Unofficial integration — it relies on TradingView's internal interfaces and may stop working when the platform updates.
Not financial advice and not a trading recommendation; it's a tooling/automation demo.
Runs locally against your own TradingView Desktop session.
